subject: SLA: monthly remedy structure, latency SLOs, and exception paths
messages:
From: Oliver James <oliver.james@nebula.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-20T09:04:00Z
Subject: SLA redlines + monthly credit cap request

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks for the draft SLA. Our procurement and legal teams ran a quick review and flagged two things we can't accept in the current form: the baseline uptime target at 99.95% and an uncapped monthly remedy that could compound quickly for larger spend months.

High level asks from Nebula: 
- Baseline uptime at 99.9% instead of 99.95% (we're running inference across hybrid infra and want a slightly looser production commitment).
- A fixed monthly credit cap equal to 25% of our committed monthly spend.
- Explicit performance SLOs: p95 inference latency < 150ms for our baseline model (our workload is latency-sensitive).
- A clear exception path for major public holidays in our EU region where agreed maintenance windows may be wider.

Attached is a redline of the SLA with procurement comments (Nebula_SLA_Redline_20270520.pdf). Can Redwood propose a narrow compromise that keeps you protected but gives us predictable financial exposure?

Oliver
Oliver James
Head of Procurement, Nebula Analytics
attachments: Nebula_SLA_Redline_20270520.pdf

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T10:17:00Z
Subject: Fwd: SLA redlines + monthly credit cap request

Laura / Ben — forwarding Nebula's comments. Key asks: 99.9% baseline (down from our standard 99.95), a 25% monthly cap, and a p95 latency SLO. They also want holiday maintenance carveouts.

My initial thinking: propose keeping 99.95% as standard but add an alternate path where for hybrid/private customers we offer 99.9% with a smaller credit ladder. Example proposal (to use as negotiation starting point):
- If they accept 99.95%: standard remedy ladder (tiered credits at incremental thresholds, cap at 100% of one month).
- If they require 99.9%: simplified ladder with lower credit percentages and an explicit monthly cap at 25% agreed in contract.
- Add explicit maintenance and holiday carveouts (define 48-hour window for pre-agreed EU holidays).
- For latency: commit to an operational target (p95 < 150ms) for the pinned model variant with a performance credit only if p95 exceeds 300ms for two consecutive reporting periods.

I'll draft a clean external response that presents both paths (standard vs hybrid exception) and frames the 25% cap as an available concession if they move to the 99.9% baseline. Ben — please flag any legal risk in that approach (especially around cumulative caps + multi-region incidents).

Thanks,
Jonas

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T08:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA redlines + monthly credit cap request

Jonas — quick notes from legal:
- We can offer a two-path SLA (99.95% standard; 99.9% 'hybrid' option) but we need to: 
  1) Cap aggregate monthly credits explicitly (25% okay for hybrid option but recommend language that excludes credits for incidents caused by: customer misconfigurations, third-party cloud provider outages, force majeure, and documented DDoS where mitigation was in our control).
  2) Keep an annual aggregate cap (e.g., no more than 3x monthly cap per rolling 12 months) — otherwise a single prolonged outage could create outsized liability.
- On latency SLOs: we can commit to operational targets but avoid financial credits tied to single-metric noise. If they want financial remedy for latency, require a repeated breach threshold and runbook confirmation (e.g., two consecutive months showing p95 > 300ms with runbook not followed).
- Maintenance carveouts: define a small set of pre-agreed holiday windows (we can accept 48hr windows up to 4x/yr if scheduled 30 days in advance).
- DocuSign: ensure the contract has an explicit acceptance of the hybrid exception path and the credit cap.

I'll draft clause language and attach examples from prior deals.

Ben
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@nebula.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-23T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA redlines + monthly credit cap request

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear redlines and context. We appreciate the hybrid deployment nuance.

Proposal we can send formally:
- Option A (Standard): 99.95% monthly availability. Tiered monthly credits; maximum remedy payout equal to 100% of your committed monthly spend for that billing period.
- Option B (Hybrid/Private): 99.9% monthly availability. Simplified monthly credit ladder and an explicit cap at 25% of committed monthly spend. This option requires acceptance of the hybrid operating appendix (brief addendum listing maintenance carveouts and customer responsibilities).
- Latency: Operational target p95 < 150ms for the pinned model. Financial remedy for latency only triggers if p95 > 300ms for two consecutive monthly reports and after runbook/triage steps are completed.
- Holiday carveouts: we will allow up to four scheduled 48-hour maintenance windows per rolling 12 months with 30 days' notice; additional unscheduled windows require mutual agreement.

I've attached a clean compromise draft (SLA_Compromise_v1.pdf) and a DocuSign envelope to accelerate if this works for you. If you'd like, we can propose a 60-day review clause post-go-live to revisit thresholds based on actual telemetry.

Next steps: confirm Option A or B and whether Nebula is comfortable with the credit caps and the review cadence. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to close details.

Best,
Laura
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
attachments: SLA_Compromise_v1.pdf
link: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/12345abcde

From: Oliver James <oliver.james@nebula.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nebula.ai
Date: 2027-05-24T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA redlines + monthly credit cap request

Laura / team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear Option A/B framing. Nebula prefers Option B (Hybrid) with the 25% monthly cap, subject to two clarifications before we sign: 
1) We need the holiday carveouts explicitly enumerated for our EU legal team (list of standard EU bank holidays + ability to nominate up to 2 additional company-specific dates per year).
2) For latency, can you make the operational target explicit in the SLO table and confirm that pinned model definition will be included as an appendix (model version + tokenization/config). We want the 60-day review clause included.

If you can update the draft with those two points we can route to our legal and procurement and aim to sign the week after next. We'll accept DocuSign once the appendix is attached.

Thanks,
Oliver

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@nebula.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-24T16:28:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA redlines + monthly credit cap request — confirmation and next steps

Oliver — great, glad Option B is directionally acceptable. Action items and timeline: 
- Ben will fold the holiday carveout language into the hybrid appendix (we'll enumerate standard EU bank holidays and allow Nebula to nominate 2 company-specific dates/year). Ben — please aim for the updated clause by tomorrow EOD.
- I'll update the SLO table to include the explicit p95 < 150ms target and appendix placeholder listing the pinned model (model name, version, tokenization, inference config).
- Laura — please prepare the DocuSign envelope with the hybrid appendix and set the review clause (60 days post-go-live) so it appears in the contract.
- Target: updated draft to Nebula by 2027-05-26; sign-off week of 2027-05-31 pending procurement review.

Thanks all — we should be able to keep the 25% monthly cap for Option B as requested, provided we keep the exclusions and the annual aggregate cap language Ben suggested. I'll include the HubSpot deal link for tracking: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/NEB-4092.

Jonas
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
